skill.name: agentix-ceo
skill.description: Orchestrate Agentix roles, tasks, workers, playbooks, and team setup through the Agentix API.
skill.summary: Manage Agentix teams, worker tasks, credentials, and playbook-driven automation from an AI assistant.
skill.author: agentix-cloud

security_audit.summary: Most external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backtick formatting, not executable shell code. The remaining confirmed issues are substantive: the skill contacts Agentix services, persists hidden credentials, handles Agentix API keys, and asks users to transmit Anthropic and GitHub secrets to remote team configuration. Remote playbooks and autopilot behavior also create a prompt-injection and autonomous-action risk surface.

remediation.issue: Sensitive credentials are stored in ~/.agentix/credentials and loaded silently across sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Use an OS credential store or encrypted file, require explicit user consent before loading secrets, and document file permissions.

remediation.issue: The skill asks users to submit Anthropic API keys and GitHub tokens to Agentix configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Require least-privilege tokens, show the exact destination host, explain retention, and support scoped or temporary credentials.

remediation.issue: Remote playbooks can influence agent behavior, including autopilot task creation and worker spawning.
remediation.suggestion: Treat fetched playbooks as untrusted data, require user confirmation for mode changes, and limit autopilot actions by default.

remediation.issue: The self-hosted path describes an unauthenticated API open on the local network.
remediation.suggestion: Add authentication for self-hosted instances or bind them to localhost with clear network exposure warnings.

content.value_statement: Coordinating AI workers across roles, tasks, and status updates can be difficult. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured Agentix operations playbook.
actual_capabilities: Guides registration, team creation, and credential setup for Agentix Cloud or self-hosted Agentix.
Reads and updates an Agentix team playbook that defines supervised or autopilot operating mode.
Creates, lists, updates, and deletes Agentix roles with role-specific system prompts.
Creates and monitors Agentix tasks from backlog through review, completion, or failure.
Starts or resumes Agentix workers for specific tasks through documented API endpoints.
Configures GitHub and Anthropic API keys for Agentix workers when the user provides them.
limitations: Requires an Agentix API endpoint and a valid team configuration before most workflows work.
Handles sensitive API keys and tokens, so users must review the trust model before use.
Does not perform work locally; it delegates work to Agentix workers and remote services.
Autopilot mode can create tasks and spawn workers without step-by-step confirmation.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Engineering Work
use_cases.description: Plan roles, create tasks, and start Agentix workers for implementation and review work.

use_cases.title: Operate a Self-Hosted Agentix Team
use_cases.description: Connect an assistant to a local Agentix instance and manage roles, tasks, workers, and events.

use_cases.title: Track Multi-Agent Progress
use_cases.description: Check task status, worker activity, and recent events for an active Agentix team.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Agentix
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up my Agentix team. Ask for only the information you need, then show me each external service involved before saving credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Review Team Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Agentix team status. Summarize running workers, blocked tasks, recent events, and actions that need my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Create Focused Work Items
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Agentix tasks for this goal. Reuse existing roles where possible and explain each role choice before creating tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Run Supervised Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a supervised Agentix delivery loop. Monitor workers, resume failed work when appropriate, and ask before creating new roles or tasks.

output_examples.input: Create a backend task and start a worker for it.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the existing backend role, creates a ready task with a clear scope, starts one worker, and reports the worker status.

output_examples.input: Show me what my Agentix team is doing.
output_examples.output: The assistant summarizes current tasks, running workers, recent events, failed jobs, and the next decision that needs user approval.

output_examples.input: Switch my team from autopilot to supervised mode.
output_examples.output: The assistant fetches the supervised playbook template, preserves custom policies, updates the team playbook, and confirms the new operating mode.

best_practices: Use supervised mode until roles, tasks, and credential handling are fully understood.
Review every external endpoint before saving credentials or sending third-party tokens.
Use least-privilege GitHub and API tokens for Agentix worker configuration.
anti_patterns: Do not share broad personal access tokens when a scoped token is enough.
Do not enable autopilot for repositories or teams without clear operating policies.
Do not point the skill at an untrusted self-hosted Agentix endpoint.

faq.question: Does this skill require Agentix Cloud?
faq.answer: No. It supports Agentix Cloud and self-hosted Agentix endpoints when configured by the user.

faq.question: Can it create and run workers?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents task run and resume endpoints for Agentix workers.

faq.question: Does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for Agentix, Anthropic, and GitHub credentials in some flows. Users should review token scope first.

faq.question: What is supervised mode?
faq.answer: Supervised mode monitors and advances existing work, but asks before planning new work or spawning workers.

faq.question: What is autopilot mode?
faq.answer: Autopilot mode lets the assistant monitor, plan, create tasks, spawn workers, review, merge, and continue looping.

faq.question: Is this safe for sensitive repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. The skill sends tokens and work instructions to Agentix services, so sensitive work needs a reviewed trust boundary.
